CWE-22.name: Path Traversal
CWE-22.description: A pathname is built from external input without neutralizing sequences such as '../', so it can resolve to a location outside the restricted directory.
CWE-22.remediation: Resolve the path against a fixed base directory, canonicalize it and reject it unless it still starts with the base directory. Prefer mapping user input to an allow-list of file names.

CWE-78.name: OS Command Injection
CWE-78.description: An operating system command is built from external input, letting an attacker run arbitrary commands with the application's privileges.
CWE-78.remediation: Do not pass user input to Runtime.exec or a shell. Use a Java API for the task, or validate the input against a strict allow-list and pass it as a separate argument to ProcessBuilder without invoking a shell.

CWE-89.name: SQL Injection
CWE-89.description: An SQL command is built from external input without neutralization, so the input can change the query's logic, read or modify data, or run administrative operations.
CWE-89.remediation: Use parameterized queries (PreparedStatement with ? placeholders, JPA named parameters, or Spring JdbcTemplate arguments). Never concatenate input into SQL. Apply least-privilege database accounts.

CWE-327.name: Broken or Risky Cryptographic Algorithm
CWE-327.description: The code uses a broken or risky cryptographic algorithm or mode (DES, RC4, ECB, old TLS versions), which can expose sensitive data.
CWE-327.remediation: Use modern authenticated encryption such as AES/GCM/NoPadding with a random 12-byte IV and 256-bit keys, and TLS 1.2+.

CWE-328.name: Weak Hash
CWE-328.description: A weak hash algorithm (MD5, SHA-1) is used where collision or preimage resistance is needed, such as for passwords or integrity checks.
CWE-328.remediation: Use SHA-256 or better for integrity, and a slow salted password hash (bcrypt, scrypt, Argon2 or PBKDF2) for passwords.

CWE-798.name: Hard-coded Credentials
CWE-798.description: Credentials such as passwords, API keys or tokens are embedded in the source code, where anyone with repository or binary access can read and reuse them.
CWE-798.remediation: Remove the secret from the code and git history, rotate it, and read it at runtime from environment variables, a secrets manager or the platform's credential store.

CWE-502.name: Deserialization of Untrusted Data
CWE-502.description: Untrusted data is deserialized with a mechanism that can instantiate arbitrary classes, enabling gadget-chain attacks up to remote code execution.
CWE-502.remediation: Do not deserialize untrusted data with ObjectInputStream, XMLDecoder or unrestricted polymorphic JSON. Use data-only formats (JSON into fixed DTOs) or apply an allow-list ObjectInputFilter.
